@ui.alertDialog.defaultButton.description: Default label for the single dismiss button in a generic alert dialog, used when the caller passes no custom button text. A confirmation/acknowledgement, like the standard OK button.

@ui.alertDialog.copyPathAria.description: aria-label for the Copy button beside the path shown in an alert dialog (for example "Path is too long"). Screen-reader-only; the visible button label is the shared "Copy" / "Copied!" pair. "Path" here means a filesystem path such as /Users/dave/photos/img.jpg. Keep it identical in wording to commands.fileCopyPath.label.

@ui.modalDialog.close.description: aria-label for the small × close button in the top-right corner of any modal dialog. Screen-reader-only; the visible glyph is ×.

@ui.popover.defaultAriaLabel.description: Default aria-label naming a popover region when the caller passes none. Generic fallback meaning a small floating panel of choices.

@ui.select.placeholder.description: Default placeholder shown in a dropdown (select) trigger before the user has picked an option.

ui.combobox.emptyText: No matches. Keep typing to use your own value.

@ui.combobox.emptyText.description: Shown in a combobox (text field with suggestions) popup when nothing matches what the user typed. Reassures them they can still enter a custom value that isn't in the suggestion list.

@ui.combobox.loadingSuggestions.description: aria-label for the in-field loading spinner while a combobox fetches its suggestion list.

@ui.combobox.showSuggestions.description: aria-label for the chevron button that opens a combobox's suggestion dropdown.

@ui.copyBox.copyAria.description: aria-label for the Copy button in a CopyBox, the box that shows a string to copy verbatim. This is the DEFAULT, used where the string is a terminal command; a caller showing something else (a file path) passes its own label. Screen-reader-only.

@ui.copyBox.copy.description: Resting label of the Copy button next to a string shown for copying (a terminal command, a file path). Tight button; keep short.

@ui.copyBox.copied.description: Brief confirmation shown on the Copy button right after the string was copied, replacing the word Copy for a couple of seconds. Tight button; keep short.

@ui.shortcutChip.customizeAria.description: Screen-reader text inside a clickable keyboard-shortcut pill that opens shortcut customization for one command. It's read right after the key the pill shows ("⌘C Customize the Copy shortcut"), so keep it a phrase that follows the key naturally.

placeholders.commandName: the name of the command whose shortcut this pill shows (for example Copy, Rename)

@ui.shortcutChip.customizeTooltip.description: Tooltip on hovering a clickable keyboard-shortcut pill, hinting that clicking it opens shortcut customization.

@ui.toast.dismissAria.description: aria-label for the × button that closes (dismisses) a toast notification.

@ui.toast.noneToFocus.description: Spoken by the screen reader (never shown) when the user runs the "Move focus to the notifications" command while no notification toast is on screen, so there's nothing for focus to move to.

@ui.toast.age.description: Small gray label at the top right of a notification toast, beside its close button, saying how long ago the notification appeared. Only shown once the toast is at least a minute old, and it counts up as time passes. Keep it very short: it shares a line with the toast's first line of text.

placeholders.durationText: how long ago, already formatted as a number plus a one-letter unit, for example 2m (minutes) or 1h (hours)

ui.loadingIcon.finalizing: All {countText} {count, plural, one {file} other {files}} loaded. Sorting your files, preparing view…

@ui.loadingIcon.finalizing.description: Loading message shown after all entries arrive, while the list is being sorted and laid out. Appears centered in a pane during a slow directory open.

placeholders.countText: how many files, already formatted for display (for example 1,234)
placeholders.count: the same number of files (drives the singular/plural form of the noun)

@ui.loadingIcon.loaded.description: Progress message shown while a directory is still loading, reporting how many entries have arrived so far. Appears centered in a pane.

placeholders.countText: how many files have loaded so far, already formatted for display (for example 1,234)
placeholders.count: the same number of files (drives the singular/plural form of the noun)

@ui.loadingIcon.loadingBackupIndex.description: Progress message shown centered in a pane, above a progress bar, while Cmdr reads a restic backup’s index before it can show the files in one of the backup’s snapshots. On a slow network drive this can take a while, so it counts up as the index loads. Use your language’s everyday word for a backup; “index” is the backup’s table of contents.

placeholders.amountText: how much of the index has loaded so far out of its total size, already worded, for example 48 MB of 312 MB

@ui.loadingIcon.backupIndexAmount.description: How much of a restic backup’s index has loaded, for example “48 MB of 312 MB”. Shown at the end of ui.loadingIcon.loadingBackupIndex, and read by screen readers as the value of the progress bar under it.

placeholders.doneText: how much has loaded so far, already formatted with its unit (e.g. 48 MB)
placeholders.totalText: the index’s total size, already formatted with its unit (e.g. 312 MB)

@ui.loadingIcon.backupIndexAria.description: Screen-reader name of the progress bar shown while a restic backup’s index loads (see ui.loadingIcon.loadingBackupIndex). Never shown. A short noun phrase naming what the bar measures.

@ui.loadingIcon.openingFolder.description: Loading message shown briefly while a folder is being opened, before its entries start arriving.

@ui.loadingIcon.loading.description: Generic loading message shown centered in a pane while content is being fetched.

ui.loadingIcon.cancelHint: Press <key></key> to cancel and go back

@ui.loadingIcon.cancelHint.description: Hint under the loading spinner telling the user how to abort a slow load. The empty <key></key> tag is where the app inserts a keyboard-key pill showing the Escape key (a styled chip); keep the tag, it has no text of its own.

placeholders.key: position of the inline Esc key pill (a styled chip the app fills in); keep the empty wrapper tag

@ui.numberInput.decrease.description: aria-label (screen-reader only) for the decrement (minus) button of a number input. Reads as an action plus the field's name.

placeholders.label: the name of the field this button adjusts, e.g. "Custom timeout"

@ui.numberInput.increase.description: aria-label (screen-reader only) for the increment (plus) button of a number input. Reads as an action plus the field's name.

placeholders.label: the name of the field this button adjusts, e.g. "Custom timeout"

@ui.confirmDialog.cancel.description: The cancelling button of a native confirmation alert that carries a checkbox (Forget server's "Also forget the saved password"). Use the word your language's macOS uses on a Cancel button.

@ui.startedElsewhere.agent.description: A line inside a confirmation dialog, or under the inline rename field, that Ask Cmdr (the app's built-in AI assistant) opened by itself. It tells the person the action wasn't theirs and that nothing happens until they confirm it. Keep the name Ask Cmdr untranslated.

@ui.startedElsewhere.aiClient.description: A line inside a confirmation dialog, or under the inline rename field, that an outside AI tool connected over MCP opened by itself. It tells the person the action wasn't theirs. Same term as the operation log's "AI client" initiator label.

ui.startedElsewhere.keysWait: The keyboard waits until you stop typing.

@ui.startedElsewhere.keysWait.description: Shown alone, or after the "started this" line, while a dialog that opened by itself ignores the keyboard, so that someone typing elsewhere can't confirm it by accident. It goes away about a second after the last key. Escape and clicks still work during this time, so don't word it as the dialog being locked.

@ui.toolAsk.allow.description: The confirming button of a dialog that asks a person to allow something an AI assistant wants to do, like opening a file or changing a setting.

@ui.toolAsk.decline.description: The safe button of the same dialog. It leaves everything as it is, and the assistant hears that the person said no.

ui.toolAsk.openFile.title: Open this file?

@ui.toolAsk.openFile.title.description: Title of a dialog asking whether an AI assistant may open a file in another app. That can run code, so it's a real question.

placeholders.name: the file's name
placeholders.app: the app macOS would open it with, like Terminal

ui.toolAsk.openFile.bodyUnknownApp: This opens {name}, and Cmdr can’t tell which app that uses.

@ui.toolAsk.openFile.bodyUnknownApp.description: The same body when macOS names no default app for the file.

ui.toolAsk.openBundle.title: Run this bundle?

@ui.toolAsk.openBundle.title.description: Title of a dialog asking whether an AI assistant may launch a macOS bundle: a folder that macOS treats as one program, like an .app.

ui.toolAsk.openBundle.body: {name} is a bundle, so opening it runs it as a program.
ui.toolAsk.setSetting.title: Change this setting?

@ui.toolAsk.setSetting.title.description: Title of a dialog asking whether an AI assistant may change one of the app's settings.

@ui.toolAsk.setSetting.oldValue.description: Caption of the first row under the setting's name in the change-a-setting dialog. The row shows the value the setting has now: a friendly name plus the stored value in code style, like TextEdit com.apple.TextEdit.

@ui.toolAsk.setSetting.newValue.description: Caption of the second row in that dialog: the value the AI assistant wants to set, shown the same way as the old value.

@ui.toolAsk.setSetting.systemDefault.description: Friendly name of the text editor setting's 'system' value in that dialog, shown before the stored value: System default system. It means F4 opens files in whatever app macOS uses for plain text. Use the wording your locale's macOS uses for a system-wide default.

@ui.toolAsk.setSetting.emptyValue.description: Stands in for a setting's value in the change-a-setting dialog when the value is empty, as in the row: Old value: nothing.

ui.toolAsk.quit.title: Quit Cmdr?

@ui.toolAsk.quit.title.description: Title of a dialog asking whether an AI assistant may quit the app.

ui.toolAsk.quit.body: This closes Cmdr. If anything’s still running, you get to decide about that first.

@ui.toolAsk.quit.body.description: Body of that dialog. Running means file operations like a copy in progress: the app asks about those separately.

ui.toolAsk.eject.title: Eject this volume?

@ui.toolAsk.eject.title.description: Title of a dialog asking whether an AI assistant may eject a disk, unmount a network share, or disconnect a phone. All of those are called a volume here.

@ui.toolAsk.eject.body.description: Body of that dialog, for one volume.

ui.toolAsk.eject.bodyWholeDisk: This ejects the whole disk {name} is on, with every volume on it.

@ui.toolAsk.eject.bodyWholeDisk.description: The same body when the whole physical disk goes, along with any other volumes it holds.

ui.toolAsk.removeServer.title: Remove this server?

@ui.toolAsk.removeServer.title.description: Title of a dialog asking whether an AI assistant may remove a server the person added by hand.

ui.toolAsk.removeServer.body: This removes {name} from your saved servers.
ui.toolAsk.indexing.enable.title: Turn indexing on?

@ui.toolAsk.indexing.enable.title.description: Title of a dialog asking whether an AI assistant may turn on drive indexing for one volume. Indexing is what makes whole-drive search fast.

ui.toolAsk.indexing.enable.body: This turns indexing on for {name} and starts scanning it.
ui.toolAsk.indexing.disable.title: Turn indexing off?

@ui.toolAsk.indexing.disable.title.description: Title of a dialog asking whether an AI assistant may turn off drive indexing for one volume.

ui.toolAsk.indexing.disable.body: This turns indexing off for {name}, and keeps what it has indexed so far.
ui.toolAsk.indexing.rescan.title: Scan this volume again?

@ui.toolAsk.indexing.rescan.title.description: Title of a dialog asking whether an AI assistant may rescan one volume from scratch for drive indexing.

ui.toolAsk.indexing.rescan.body: This scans all of {name} again, which can take a while.
ui.toolAsk.indexing.forget.title: Forget this index?

@ui.toolAsk.indexing.forget.title.description: Title of a dialog asking whether an AI assistant may delete what drive indexing knows about one volume.

ui.toolAsk.indexing.forget.body: This deletes the index of {name}. The files on it stay where they are.

@ui.toolAsk.indexing.forget.body.description: Body of that dialog. Only Cmdr's own search data goes, never any of the person's files.

ui.dialogBoundary.closedToast: That dialog ran into a problem, so we closed it. Please try again.

@ui.dialogBoundary.closedToast.description: Toast shown when any dialog in the app broke unexpectedly, while opening, in use, or while closing. The app has already closed the dialog and put keyboard focus back on the file list, so the person can simply open it again. "That dialog" is deliberately generic: the toast doesn't know the dialog's name.
